How to Identify Roof Damage During Summer in Pennsylvania

18 July 2024 Roof Repair

Summer can be a challenging time for roofs in Pennsylvania, with high temperatures and frequent storms taking their toll. Identifying roof damage early can save homeowners from costly repairs and ensure their homes remain protected throughout the season. Here’s a comprehensive guide on how to spot and address summer roof damage.

Common Signs of Summer Roof Damage Pennsylvania | Signs of Roof Damage

Cracked or Curled Shingles

Cracked or curled shingles are a common sign of heat damage. Prolonged exposure to high temperatures can cause asphalt shingles to become brittle and crack, or their edges to curl upwards. This damage can compromise the roof’s ability to protect against water infiltration, leading to leaks.

Blistering

Blistering occurs when trapped moisture beneath the shingles heats up, causing the surface to bubble. These blisters can pop, leaving the roof exposed to the elements. Look for raised sections or bubbles on the shingles, as these indicate blistering that needs to be addressed.

Granule Loss

Asphalt shingles are coated with granules that protect them from UV rays. Excessive heat can cause these granules to loosen and fall off. Check your gutters and downspouts for granule accumulation and inspect your roof for bald spots where granules are missing, as this can lead to significant damage.

Fading or Discoloration

Constant exposure to sunlight can cause shingles to fade or discolor. This not only affects the aesthetic appeal but also indicates UV damage. Look for patches of your roof that appear lighter or different in color compared to the rest, which signifies potential deterioration.

How to Inspect Your Roof for Summer Damage

Ground Inspection Tips

From the ground, look for visible signs of damage such as missing, cracked, or curled shingles. Use binoculars if necessary to get a closer view. Pay special attention to areas around chimneys, vents, and skylights, as these are common spots for damage.

Attic Inspection Tips

Inspect your attic for signs of water infiltration, such as moisture stains, mold growth, or damaged insulation. Check for any signs of daylight coming through the roof, which indicates gaps or holes that need immediate attention.

Safety Tips for Roof Inspection

If you decide to inspect the roof yourself, always prioritize safety. Use a sturdy ladder and wear slip-resistant shoes. Avoid walking on the roof to prevent further damage and personal injury. If in doubt, hire a professional roofer to conduct the inspection.

Repairing Summer Roof Damage

Replacing Damaged Shingles

Cracked, curled, or blistered shingles should be replaced to prevent leaks and further damage. Carefully remove the damaged shingles, apply roofing cement to the replacement shingles, secure them with roofing nails, and seal the edges with more cement.

Addressing Granule Loss

Significant granule loss may require a roof inspection and potentially a partial or full roof replacement. Contact a professional roofer to assess the extent of the damage and consider applying a protective coating to existing shingles if the damage is minimal.

Repairing Warped Roof Decks

Warped or sagging roof decks compromise the structural integrity of your home. Inspect the attic for signs of warping and remove damaged sections of the roof deck. Install new decking material and re-shingle the repaired area.

Recoloring or Replacing Faded Shingles

While fading is mostly cosmetic, severely discolored shingles may indicate UV damage. For minor fading, consider applying a roof coating that can restore color and add protection. For extensive discoloration, replace the faded shingles with new ones.

Preventative Measures for Summer Roof Damage

Improve Attic Ventilation

Proper attic ventilation helps regulate roof temperature, reducing the risk of heat damage. Install ridge vents or soffit vents to enhance airflow and ensure your attic insulation is adequate to prevent heat buildup.

Use Reflective Roofing Materials

Reflective roofing materials can reduce heat absorption, keeping your roof cooler. Consider installing cool roofing materials that reflect more sunlight or applying reflective roof coatings to your existing shingles.

Clean Gutters and Downspouts

Ensure your gutters and downspouts are clean and free of debris. Clogged gutters can cause water to back up and seep under the roof’s edge, leading to damage. Regular cleaning helps maintain proper water flow and prevents overflow during storms.

Trim Overhanging Foliage

Overhanging branches can rub against shingles and cause damage. Trim branches away from your roof to minimize this risk. Regular maintenance of nearby trees helps protect your roof from potential harm during storms.

Impact of Summer Heat on Different Roofing Materials

Asphalt Shingles

Asphalt shingles are more susceptible to heat damage, becoming brittle and losing granules under extreme temperatures. Regular inspection and maintenance are crucial to extending their lifespan.

Wood Shakes and Shingles

Wood shingles can dry out and lose their natural oils when exposed to summer heat, leading to cracking and warping. Proper treatment and coatings can help maintain their durability.

Metal Roofs

Metal roofs are highly resistant to heat and can withstand extreme temperatures. However, improper installation can lead to condensation and increase the potential for rust and corrosion. Ensure proper installation and maintenance to avoid these issues.

Flat Roofing Materials

Flat roofs made of materials like TPO, EPDM, and modified bitumen are designed to expand and contract with temperature changes. Prolonged exposure to summer heat can cause creases and cracks, affecting their protective ability. Regular inspection and maintenance are essential.

How a Heat-Damaged Roof Can Affect Your Home

Increased Energy Bills

A heat-damaged roof can cause the temperature inside your home to rise, making your HVAC system work harder. This leads to higher energy bills. Poor insulation can worsen this issue by allowing heat to enter your home more quickly.

Roof Leaks

Heat-damaged roofs are more prone to leaks. Moisture can easily penetrate cracked or lifted shingles, leading to water damage. Addressing these issues promptly can prevent further damage and costly repairs.

Mold and Algae Growth

Hot air condenses, creating humidity that makes your attic and roof a breeding ground for mold and algae. These can cause health issues for your family. Regular inspections and maintenance can help prevent this problem.

When to Call a Professional

Signs You Need Professional Help

If you notice extensive damage, such as large areas of cracked or missing shingles, significant granule loss, or structural issues like a warped roof deck, it’s time to call a professional. DIY repairs may not address the underlying problems and can lead to further damage.

Choosing the Right Roofing Contractor

When selecting a roofing contractor, look for local professionals with good reviews and proper licensing. Contact us for a thorough inspection and reliable repairs to keep your roof in top condition throughout the summer.

By staying vigilant and taking proactive measures, you can protect your roof from summer damage and ensure the longevity and safety of your home.
